items.question_text: You need to add a group of new users to Cloud Identity. Some of the users already have existing Google accounts. You want to follow one of Google's recommended practices and avoid conflicting accounts. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Google's recommended practice for resolving account conflicts when migrating to Cloud Identity is to invite the user to transfer their existing consumer account.

This process allows the organization to convert the personal Google account into a managed account while preserving access rights and data, thereby avoiding the complexity of duplicate accounts.

choices.text: Invite the user to transfer their existing account.
Invite the user to use an email alias to resolve the conflict.
Tell the user that they must delete their existing account.
Tell the user to remove all personal email from the existing account.

items.question_text: You need to manage a Cloud Spanner instance for best query performance. Your instance in production runs in a single Google Cloud region. You need to improve performance in the shortest amount of time. You want to follow Google best practices for service configuration. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Google Cloud Spanner best practices recommend maintaining high-priority CPU utilization below 65% for single-region instances to ensure stable performance and headroom.
Exceeding this threshold indicates that the instance requires more compute capacity, so adding nodes is the correct scaling action.
The 45% threshold applies to multi-region instances, making options A and B incorrect for this specific scenario.

choices.text: Create an alert in Cloud Monitoring to alert when the percentage of high priority CPU utilization reaches 45%. If you exceed this threshold, add nodes to your instance.

Create an alert in Cloud Monitoring to alert when the percentage of high priority CPU utilization reaches 45%. Use database query statistics to identify queries that result in high CPU usage, and then rewrite those queries to optimize their resource usage.

items.question_text: Your company has an internal application for managing transactional orders. The application is used exclusively by employees in a single physical location. The application requires strong consistency, fast queries, and ACID guarantees for multi-table transactional updates. The first version of the application is implemented in PostgreSQL, and you want to deploy it to the cloud with minimal code changes. Which database is most appropriate for this application?
items.solution_text:
Cloud SQL is the most appropriate choice because it provides a fully managed PostgreSQL environment, ensuring minimal code changes for an existing PostgreSQL application.
It natively supports ACID transactions and strong consistency required for multi-table updates, whereas BigQuery and Datastore are not relational databases suitable for this workload.
While Cloud Spanner offers ACID compliance, Cloud SQL is the standard lift-and-shift solution for single-location applications to preserve the exact PostgreSQL interface without architectural overhead.

choices.text: BigQuery
Cloud SQL
Cloud Spanner
Cloud Datastore

items.question_text: You are assigned to maintain a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster named 'dev' that was deployed on Google Cloud. You want to manage the GKE configuration using the command line interface (CLI). You have just downloaded and installed the Cloud SDK. You want to ensure that future CLI commands by default address this specific cluster What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To configure a default cluster for gcloud commands, you must set the 'container/cluster' property using the 'gcloud config set' command.
Option A correctly uses 'gcloud config set container/cluster dev' to establish this default context.
The other options involve incorrect commands for setting defaults or non-existent configuration files.

choices.text: Use the command gcloud config set container/cluster dev.
Use the command gcloud container clusters update dev.
Create a file called gke.default in the ~/.gcloud folder that contains the cluster name.
Create a file called defaults.json in the ~/.gcloud folder that contains the cluster name.

items.question_text: The sales team has a project named Sales Data Digest that has the ID acme-data-digest. You need to set up similar Google Cloud resources for the marketing team but their resources must be organized independently of the sales team. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Option C is correct because Google Cloud projects are the fundamental unit for organizing resources and applying Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies. Creating a separate project ensures that the marketing team's resources are isolated from the sales team, preventing cross-team access conflicts and maintaining independent billing and configuration management. Options A, B, and D fail to provide this structural separation by attempting to share the existing project or misuse project lienis.

choices.text: Grant the Project Editor role to the Marketing team for acme-data-digest.
Create a Project Lien on acme-data-digest and then grant the Project Editor role to the Marketing team.
Create another project with the ID acme-marketing-data-digest for the Marketing team and deploy the resources there.
Create a new project named Marketing Data Digest and use the ID acme-data-digest. Grant the Project Editor role to the Marketing team.
